struck: The IRS puts them in the same list as homeowners insurance, utilities and internet service, which Grand Strand condo dues often include.
use: The IRS lists them with homeowners insurance, utilities and internet service, and most Horry County condos for sale say their dues include those.

pattern: \ba little less (?:in )?the first year\b|\$364 a year for 27\.5 years
struck: A $10,000 share of a roof assessment on a condo you rent out is deducted at about $364 a year for 27.5 years, a little less in the first year.
use: Example: a $10,000 share of a roof assessment on a condo you rent out is deducted at about $364 a year in each full year, less in the first and last years, over 27.5 years from when the new roof is in service.

struck: A personal day is a day you, a co-owner or a family member uses the unit. Family means spouse, brothers and sisters, parents and grandparents, children and grandchildren.
use: A personal day is a day you, a co-owner or a relative uses it (unless the relative rents it at a fair price as their main home), a day anyone pays less than a fair rent, and a day used under a swap.

struck: If you never use it, every day of the year counts toward the rental side, and costs while it sits empty for rent are deductible.
use: If you never use it yourself, nothing is split: all of the dues are a rental expense, including months it sits empty while you hold it out for rent.

struck: For a self-employed owner who qualifies, Form 8829 has a line for operating expenses not on its other lines, so the business share of the dues goes there.
use: (cut it: no IRS source names association dues as a home office expense; say only that employees get no deduction and that a self-employed owner who qualifies splits whole-home costs by the business share)

struck: South Carolina follows the same rules.
use: South Carolina starts from the federal figures, so the same rules on dues, rental days and depreciation apply on the state return.

struck: On the Grand Strand the rental answer is the common one.
use: Only about 1 in 5 Horry County condo units is taxed at the 4 percent rate for its owner's legal residence. The rest are taxed at 6 percent, the rate for rentals, second homes and any home whose owner has not claimed the legal-residence rate.

use: Inside the city, about 1 in 11 condo units is taxed as its owner's legal residence. The rest are taxed at 6 percent, the rate for rentals, second homes and any home whose owner has not claimed the legal-residence rate.

use: About 6 in 10 Horry County condo units have their tax bill mailed to an address outside South Carolina.

pattern: \bexpect the county to see\b|\b(?:holds|keeps?) (?:the 4 percent rate )?(?:as long as|if)\b[^.]{0,60}\b72 days\b
struck: South Carolina's 4 percent rate for a legal residence holds if the home is not rented for more than 72 days in a year. A main-home owner who rents and deducts dues should expect the county to see it.
use: A legal residence keeps the 4 percent rate only while the owner still qualifies and rents it no more than 72 days in a calendar year. The assessor may ask for the owner's Schedule E.

struck: Our comparison: the dues you cannot deduct are many times the tax you can. On a Myrtle Beach condo taxed as a rental, the dues are still almost 4 times the tax.
use: On a Myrtle Beach condo that is its owner's legal residence, a year of dues at the middle for condos for sale in ZIP 29577 (about $9,300) is about 11 times the 2026 tax bill of the middle-valued such condo in the city (about $830). The tax counts on the federal return if you itemize; the dues never do.
